items.summary: Recommendation: maintain containment-only execution and preserve the CRO/product items as deferred backlog. Evidence: 197 approved proposals lack execution, 46 failure follow-ups remain open, 29 deployed improvements await measurement, only 1 outcome is proven, and the authoritative candidate list is empty. Revenue is limited to $4.92 aggregate commission for 2026-09-21 with $0 site-attributed; ROI, margin, causal lift, and cost-to-learn remain unknown. Smallest next step: continue existing measurement, attribution reconciliation, failed-work repair-or-close, and legal/security evidence work. Owner decision: authorize the prepared Woot permission request after human-counsel review, or keep it unsent.

CRO and product recommendations are preserved as deferred concepts only: control-plane lineage, lifecycle/measurement visibility, queue-capacity reporting, accessible CTA patterns, and validated repository prototypes. No new proposal, experiment, dependency, telemetry, GitHub adoption, or change request is justified while containment controls remain active. Existing failures must remain isolated until lineage, root cause, validation, rollback, deduplication, and explicit disposition are documented.

Recommendation: keep SearchWoot private. Official Woot documentation establishes API access mechanics but not rights for public display, storage, derivatives, alerts, or monetization; all four legal checklist tasks remain open, and security, accuracy, attribution, measurement, and owner gates are incomplete. The smallest next step is the existing consolidated read-only evidence bundle and field-level rights matrix; no external request should be sent without the owner decision and human-counsel review.
